newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire said asking UN condemn "foreign aggression".
newsitem.headline: Zaire said asking UN condemn "foreign aggression".

text.p: Zaire has asked the United Nations Security Council to condemn what it calls an attack by foreign troops on its territory, a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters Zaire's Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda "has written a letter to the president of the Security Council, requesting condemnation of the alleged aggression against Zaire by foreign troops".
It was not immediately clear when the letter was sent, or whether Kinshasa had requested a formal Security Council meeting on the fighting in east Zaire.
Kamanda was in Paris on Monday for talks with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on the situation in the Great Lakes region.

Tutsi-led rebels have been battling the mercenary-backed Zaire army since October and hold a strip of eastern Zaire extending from the borders with Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba province.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting alongside the ethnic Tutsis.
The rebels say their goal is to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has ruled Zaire since 1965. Mobutu has ruled out negotiations, vowing to defeat the rebels on the battlefield.
